payload.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

ambiguities: Whether the answer should specify all maximizing x values (the entire argmax set) or just one representative maximizing x
Whether the maximal value means an actual maximum over all real x (attained) versus an upper bound/supremum
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The maximum is intended to be attained by at least one real x (not merely a supremum)
The summation is finite because n is finite
No restriction is placed on the sign of x; all real x are allowed

domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1
k is an integer with 1 less than or equal to k less than or equal to n
x ranges over all real numbers
floor is the usual greatest integer function mapping real inputs to integers
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, define f_n(x) = floor of (n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor of (k times x) divided by k). Determine the set of real x that maximize f_n(x) over all real numbers x, and determine the maximum value of f_n(x).
quantifier_order: Fix an integer n with n greater than 1
There exists a real x such that the expression at x is at least the expression at every real y
For all real y, compare the expression value at x versus y

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter used in the definition of the objective function and in the summation range

variables.name: x
variables.role: free variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index ranging from 1 to n

witness_dependencies: The maximizing real number(s) x can depend on the chosen integer n
The claimed maximal value depends on n
